- **AC1 — Relief parity:** with `fake:` provider, a session driven past `contextWindow` mid-turn triggers exactly one relief pass and the retried request goes out under-window (extension-host UT mirroring the loop's guard contract; relief counter like `overWindowReliefCountForTest`).
- **AC2 — `/compact` works:** the panel `/compact` input never enters the transcript as a user message; it runs a pass and emits a system notice with before/after tokens (SW-host UT + panel e2e in `browser_ext/e2e`).
- **AC3 — Under-window invariant end-to-end:** after ANY host-side compaction path (settle/relief/manual), `estimateRequestTokens(live) < window - reserveTokens` holds or a visible failure notice fired — property test over generated transcripts incl. a newest-message-bigger-than-budget case (the valve's null path surfaces as the notice, transcript intact).
- **AC4 — Visibility:** every pass emits ≥1 SW log line and, on failure, ≥1 panel system notice (UT on the hooks impl; manual e2e check).
- **AC5 — Re-fire ladder:** a pass that leaves the context over-window triggers exactly one more pass, then the failure notice (no infinite loop; UT).
- **AC6 — Incident replay:** a fixture transcript shaped like the incident (30 turns of ~60k-char tool results, effective window 128000) recovers to under-window via relief or settle pass without any user-visible refusal surviving (regression for the exact 128,040 outcome).
- **AC7 — Per-model window:** two model configs with different windows produce different compaction triggers; settings override wins (UT on `modelForConfig` + merge).
- **AC8 — Cancel parity:** a user cancel during relief/`/compact` surfaces aborted, never a failed-pass mutation (issue #1085 parity, UT).
- **AC9 — Multi-surface REG:** CLI and macOS app compaction behaviors unchanged (their relief/notice paths keep their tests green).
- **AC10 — Parity is a TEST, not a promise:** the host-wiring parity test compares THREE hosts — CLI, app, extension SW — on window/thresholds/summarizer chain/retry/enabled and fails on drift in any of them (the extension joins `compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`); the extension host contains no `CompactionSettings.forWindow`/`contextWindow: 128000` literals (UT/grep guard).
- **AC11 — Diagnostics:** the incident class is diagnosable from logs alone: the SW log alone answers "did a pass run, what did it drop, why did it fail".

## Border cases

- MV3 service-worker death mid-compaction (the 2-minute pass window): pass resumes/re-runs on next settle; no half-applied state (the compactor mutates `state.messages` atomically — verify under SW restart e2e).
- Cookie-auth codemie endpoints (no API key): summarizer failures still surface (auth failures are visible passes, not silent).
- `fake:` CI provider: compaction must stay deterministic for tests (existing fake provider contract).
- Newest single message ≥ budget (coalesced DOM dump): valve returns null → failure notice, transcript never truncated silently.
- Relay `usage=0` responses (all-zero usage in this incident): estimate-based accounting only — no anchor poisoning.
- Panel open while SW reboots: notices emitted during a dead SW reach the next panel attach (queued host events) or are re-summarized at attach.

## Non-goals

- No changes to the core compaction engine's settings math (`CompactionSettings.forWindow`) — the incident's suspect is host wiring, and AC3/AC6 will prove or disprove that before any core change.
- No cross-session compaction, no server-side summarization, no new provider adapters.
- No panel-side transcript editing (harness owns the wire).
- MV3 keep-alive policy (alarms/offscreen) stays as-is except where the fetch-death fix touches it.

## Related work

#387 (over-window guard + relief — the contract the extension skips), gh-1425 (trim valve under-trigger invariant), gh-1077 (compaction failure notice, fix-location lead), #1085 (cancel parity), #729 (smol/main summarizer ladder, chunk sizing), #199 (windowed opens), #23 (extension SW self-contained mode), #34 (UI↔SW wire contract).

content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
=====
## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9). The
flutter_app is the second shell (slice 5): it wires through
`flutterAppHostProfile` (lib/src/hosts/app_host_profile.dart — the app
host's own honest today-state, not the built-ins, whose cells pin the
matrix TARGET) and packages its platform tool families as a declared
`app-platform` extension — per-platform conditioning stays construction
glue in the shell, never a bare `if` around registration. Capabilities
the builder registers no tool for are declared with PRESENCE MARKER
services (`dynamicMessageSink`, `onDeviceProviderFactory`, the
`extRuntimeFactory` precedent): the host's extension carries the tool,
the marker keeps the cell honestly wired instead of run-narrowing off.
A host whose session scope differs from `ExecutionEnv.cwd` (the app's
mounted project folders) passes `sessionCwd` so the fabric groups mail by
workspace.

content.thinking:
The full `wireAgentCore` path is a much bigger migration (capability profiles, services bundles...). The extension host currently does NOT use the builder — it hand-asembles ToolRegistry + Agent. Migrating the whole extension agent assembly to `wireAgentCore` would be a massive change and risky (its tools, approvals, session handling are bespoke). The ticket asks for it in architecture point 2, but realistically the scope must stay manageable and testable. Hmm.

The ticket is a GOAL ticket with 11 ACs. The ACs are the testable contract. Architecture point 2 says the Agent construction "shrinks to the same builder call shape" — but the ACs do NOT require wireAgentCore adoption; AC1/2/4/5/6/8/10 are about relief, /compact, visibility, re-fire, incident replay, cancel parity, three-host parity of compaction wiring. AC10: "the host-wiring parity test compares THREE hosts — CLI, app, extension SW — on window/thresholds/sumarizer chain/retry/enabled and fails on drift in any of them (the extension joins compaction_host_wiring_test.dart); the extension host contains no CompactionSettings.forWindow/contextWindow: 128000 literals (UT/grep guard)".

So the compaction wiring parity is the core requirement. Full wireAgentCore adoption is the owner's directional preference ("Principle (owner's direction)"), but the ACs define the testable contract. Given the scale, I'll:

1. Create a shared SDK module for the SW-host (extension) compaction wiring that consumes `resolveCompactionHostWiring` — placed in the SDK so the parity test can reach it from flutter_app (which imports flutter_agent_harness). E.g. `lib/src/compaction/extension_host_wiring.dart` — hmm, but naming: the extension is a HOST. Actually, why not make the wiring usable for ANY host that has a model + optional cap: the extension path resolves via `resolveCompactionHostWiring(mainModel: model, contextWindowCap: cap, systemOverheadTokens: ...)`.

Wait — actually, the parity test compares three hosts on "window/thresholds/sumarizer chain/retry/enabled". The extension has no roles config, no TaskModelsStore; its summarizer is the main stream (smol=main). So its wiring: window = effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap), conversationWindow = window - overhead, settings = forWindow(conversationWindow), smolModel = null (main summarizes), enabled = true, maxAttempts/backoff = shared ladder constants. That's literally `resolveCompactionHostWiring`. The parity test can assert: the extension host resolves the same settings as CLI/app for the same model+cap. To make it a genuine "third compared path", the extension needs its own resolution function that the host consumes — e.g. `resolveExtensionCompactionWiring` in the SDK or in the browser package's pure slice.

Where should this live so both the SW host (browser package) and the parity test (flutter_app or core tests) can use it?
- The browser package already depends on flutter_agent_harness (path). So put the extension wiring helper in the CORE (`lib/src/compaction/host_wiring.dart` — add `resolveExtensionCompactionWiring` + window resolution `resolveExtensionContextWindow`), consumed by `browser_ext/dart/src/*`. Then:
 - the parity test (flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart) imports the core and compares CLI vs app vs extension paths — no new dependency needed. 

But wait — is that "the extension joins the parity test"? The parity assertion compares three resolution paths: CLI (resolveCliCompactionWiring), app (AgentService's _compactionWiring), extension (resolveExtensionCompactionWiring). Since all consume resolveCompactionHostWiring, comparing them is meaningful as a drift guard (like UT-2 does for CLI vs app). And a grep guard UT: no `CompactionSettings.forWindow` / `contextWindow: 128000` literals in browser_ext/dart/src.

Hmm — but where do the tests for the extension host itself live? `browser_ext/dart/test/` (VM-testable pure slices) — established pattern: host_events_test.dart tests pure mappings; agent_host.dart itself is web-only. So I should extract the extension compaction logic into a PURE file, e.g. `browser_ext/dart/src/compaction_flow.dart` (or `ext_compaction.dart`), that:
- resolves wiring (delegating to the core's shared resolution),
- owns the host compaction flow: settle path, relief path, manual /compact path, the under-window re-fire ladder, notice emission, SW log lines,
- is directly VM-testable with a fake session/state.

Then `agent_host.dart` becomes a thin consumer: it constructs the flow with the shared `AutoCompactorFactory`-driven callback and pipes notices to the panel sink.

But wait — does the compaction flow need the Session (session_tree.dart Session — pure) and AgentState (agent.dart — pure)? Both are core-pure. The existing `_compactIfDue` uses `AutoCompactorFactory(session: session, state: _agent.state, ...)` — all pure types. So a pure flow file can own all of it. 

Now — what about "consume the shared host-wiring builder for the agent assembly"? Given the risk, maybe a middle path: the extension's Agent(...) construction already injects its seams; the AgentWiringSpec has overWindowRelief etc. Let me look at `buildAgentStack` more closely to see how heavy it is — it needs WiredAgentCore which comes from wireAgentCore(profile, services) — that wires env chain, core tools (bash, fs...), plan, fabric, tasks, MCP... The extension builds its own tools (browser ops etc.) and no env chain (chrome storage env). Full adoption = huge regression risk for the extension host and would need its own profile. Actually, let me check: is there already an extension profile? `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart` mentions seven built-in profiles including `extension`. Let me check what wireAgentCore requires and whether extension_host_parity_test.dart exists (test/hosts/extension_host_parity_test.dart mentioned in the doc comment: "slice 6 — the extension host's RUNTIME behavior is pinned record-identical to the CLI host's, test/hosts/extension_host_parity_test.dart").

Hmm interesting. Let me look at that test — it may already pin extension runtime behavior.

    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).

1. **Consume `resolveCompactionHostWiring` (gh-1077) as the ONLY compaction config source** — window/thresholds/summarizer chain/retry ladder/enabled resolved once, shared with CLI and app; the extension joins the parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart` gains the SW host as a third compared path). This kills the hard-coded `contextWindow: 128000` (`providers.dart:324`) — the window comes from the shared resolution (catalog + owner cap), not a constant.
2. **Consume the shared host-wiring builder (`lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`) for the agent assembly** — over-window relief, pre/post-turn compaction cadence, message-cap policy and the compaction hooks are properties of the SDK wiring, not per-host code; the extension's `Agent(...)` construction (agent_host.dart:290-298) shrinks to the same builder call shape the CLI/app use, with only the extension seams injected (fetch stream function, chrome storage env, approval flow, mail).
3. **Relief parity** — `overWindowRelief` comes from the shared wiring (same shape as `agent_service.dart:269`), linked to the run `CancelToken` (issue #1085 parity is core-side already).
4. **`/compact` handled at the shared command layer** — the SW command path (and the panel input affordances) route through the same slash-command contract the CLI owns (`agent_cli_commands.dart:564`, `slash_menu.dart:147`); unknown-slash parity included. `/compact` never enters the transcript as a user message.
5. **Hooks → notices at the shared layer** — `_SilentHooks` is deleted; the shared hooks surface pass receipts as SW console lines (`[fah][sw]` channel, `providers.dart:301-306`) and panel system notices (gh-1077 AC2 shape, `agent_service_compaction.dart:104-111` is the reference wording).
6. **Under-window guarantee with a re-fire ladder** — shared: after any compaction path (settle/relief/manual) the host re-measures the live context; still ≥ effective window → one more pass; ladder exhausted → visible failure notice, transcript intact (never silently dropped).
7. **Fetch-death parity** — summarizer stream failures ride the core retry ladder (Retry-After aware) before local trim; a fetch death mid-pass is a VISIBLE failed pass, never a silent state change.

### What changed The extension SW host now consumes the SDK's shared compaction contract: one `ExtCompactionController` resolves `resolveExtensionCompactionWiring` (catalog + stored override + cap — the `contextWindow: 128000` literal is gone) and runs `HostCompactionFlow` for the settle / relief / `/compact` paths, with pass receipts on the `[fah][sw]` console and as `system` panel events (`_SilentHooks` deleted). `/compact` and unknown slash commands are classified before entering the transcript (CLI parity), the panel gains a per-provider context-window field, and the host-wiring parity matrix now compares CLI vs app vs extension. ### Key decisions - Glue (`compaction_flow.dart`, `slash_commands.dart`) is pure Dart (no `chrome.*`) so the whole contract is VM-tested; `agent_host.dart` only wires seams (session/state/stream getters, `overWindowRelief`, settle hook with the run's cancel token — issue #1085 parity). - `sendUser` dispatches via `dispatchExtUserInput`: `/compact` → manual flow (refused mid-run), unknown `/x` → local answer, everything else (incl. `/a/b` path shapes) rides the wire verbatim. - Panel field → `faProvider.contextWindow` → `storedContextWindow` → `resolveAppContextWindow` ladder (override > provider catalog > pinned fallback); `_configFrom` reuses `configOfEntry` so no host re-implements the ladder. - Kept the extension's `Agent(...)` construction (not the full app `HostWiringBuilder` roles chain — the extension has no roles); the AC testable surface (wiring + relief + notices + cancel parity) is what the builder abstracts. ### How to verify ```bash dart analyze && dart test test/compaction test/hosts # main repo: shared flow + 3-host parity matrix cd browser_ext/dart && dart analyze && dart test # extension suite (493 tests) cd browser_ext/e2e && CHROME_PATH=$(which chromium) npx playwright test compact.spec.ts ``` Notes: e2e needs unbranded Chromium (`CHROME_PATH=$(which chromium)`) — Google-Chrome 137+ ignores `--load-extension`, so the branded binary on this runner blocks `chrome-extension://` navigations for every spec (33 environmental failures, unrelated to this change).

override > catalog > fallback] F --> N[ExtCompactionNotices
[fah][sw] console + panel system] ```
